body:
Independent fresh-context reviews of the exact head `16bdeb5b60db18370fb4247dcbafac3fd478c183`, by two models of different families, each in a fresh read-only context that did not author the change.

**Both verdicts: APPROVE WITH NITS — no P0 findings, no P1 findings.**

The reviews drove three rounds of fixes, each with a regression test that fails against the pre-change code:

- A response the gateway does not understand (a body that is not an object, or one whose `models` is not a list) was taken for a catalogue that holds no models. It replaced the last good catalogue, and the endpoints went back to answering with an empty list and with a model that is not supported — the outage this change set out to end. Such a response is a failure now.
- A catalogue that was fetched and holds no models was never cached, so every request asked the upstream again.
- The two checks the cache makes before it waits for the lock, and the expiry of a cached catalogue, were not held by any test; the reviewer showed that removing any of them left the suite green. Each now has a test, and the mutations the reviews used are caught.

What the reviews verified, against an independently written model of the intended behaviour: the last good catalogue is served while the upstream is down; a failure is never cached as an empty catalogue; a burst of concurrent requests causes one upstream call per feature; one slow feature does not block the others; the model list, the image endpoint and the image path of the chat endpoint answer `503 catalog_unavailable` when the catalogue is unavailable, while a genuinely unsupported model still answers `400 model_not_supported`.

The `CI` and `dco` checks are green on this head.
